title: Decimals
summary: Find tenths and hundredths on the number line, and see how decimals are written and read.
guide: If we split the space from 0 to 1 into 10 equal parts, each part is one {{term:tenth}}: {{frac:1/10}}. Three parts make {{frac:3/10}}.

We can also write {{frac:3/10}} as {{num:0.3}}. The dot in this number is the {{term:decimal-point}}. Whole numbers go to the left of the point, and the first digit to its right shows tenths. We read {{num:0.3}} as "zero point three" or "three tenths", and {{num:1.3}} as "one point three". In Iran the decimal point is written as a slash (۰/۳) and in Afghanistan as a comma (۰,۳), which is why fractions in this academy are always stacked, one number above the other.
If we split each tenth into 10 equal parts again, each part is one {{term:hundredth}}: {{frac:1/100}}, written {{num:0.01}}. The second digit after the point shows hundredths.
Hundredths are tiny, so sometimes we zoom in: the top line shows the whole number line, and the coloured piece is the part that is magnified below.
Tap the line to place a point. You can drag a point, or tap it and move it with the arrow keys.

engine.label-line: Number line: tap to place a point

place-tenths.title: Seven tenths
place-tenths.prompt: The space from 0 to 1 is split into 10 equal parts. First predict: is {{num:0.7}} nearer to 0 or to 1? Then place a point on {{num:0.7}}.
place-tenths.hint: {{num:0.7}} means seven tenths, {{frac:7/10}}. Move 7 parts along from 0.
place-tenths.success: Well done! {{num:0.7}} is the same as {{frac:7/10}}: seven of ten equal parts.
place-tenths.why: Is {{num:0.7}} nearer to 0 or to 1? How do you know?
place-tenths.model: Nearer to 1. From {{num:0.7}} to 1 there are only three tenths left, but from 0 to {{num:0.7}} there are seven tenths.

feedback.count: Place one point on the line. Just tap the line.
feedback.too-big: Too far. Move just 7 parts along from 0.
feedback.too-small: Go a little further. {{num:0.7}} is 7 parts along from 0.

read-decimal.title: Write the point as a decimal
read-decimal.prompt: What number does the point on the line show? Write it as a decimal, using a decimal point.
read-decimal.hint: Count how many parts past 0 the point is. There are no wholes, so write 0 before the point.
read-decimal.why: Why is {{num:0.3}} less than 1, but 3 is more than 1?
read-decimal.model: In {{num:0.3}} the digit before the point is 0, so there are no wholes, and the 3 after the point means three tenths. But 3 with no point means three wholes.

feedback.empty: You haven't written a number yet, or it isn't written as a decimal. Write 0, then the point, then the tenths digit.
feedback.too-big: Your number is bigger than the point. If you wrote 3, that means three wholes! Don't forget the decimal point.
feedback.too-small: Your number is smaller than the point. Count the parts from 0 again.

compare.title: Which is bigger?
compare.prompt: Here the piece from {{num:0.4}} to {{num:0.6}} is magnified, and each small part is one hundredth. The point already on the line shows {{num:0.5}}. First predict: which is bigger, {{num:0.45}} or {{num:0.5}}? Then place a point on {{num:0.45}} to check your prediction.
compare.hint: {{num:0.45}} means 45 hundredths. Start at {{num:0.4}} (40 hundredths) and move 5 small parts along.
compare.success: Well done! {{num:0.45}} is to the left of {{num:0.5}}, so it is smaller.
compare.why: Some people think {{num:0.45}} is bigger because 45 is bigger than 5. What is their mistake?
compare.model: {{num:0.5}} means 5 tenths, which is 50 hundredths, and 45 hundredths is less than 50 hundredths. We compare decimals digit by digit, starting with the tenths: 4 tenths is less than 5 tenths.

feedback.too-big: Your point is past {{num:0.45}}. Move just 5 small parts along from {{num:0.4}}.
feedback.too-small: Go a little further. You need to move 5 small parts along from {{num:0.4}}.

hundredths-zoom.title: Hundredths under a magnifier
hundredths-zoom.prompt: On the top line, the piece between {{num:1.2}} and {{num:1.3}} is coloured, and it is magnified below. Each small part is one hundredth. Place a point on {{num:1.25}}.
hundredths-zoom.hint: {{num:1.25}} means one whole, 2 tenths and 5 hundredths. Start at {{num:1.2}} and move 5 small parts along.
hundredths-zoom.success: Great! {{num:1.25}} is exactly halfway between {{num:1.2}} and {{num:1.3}}.
hundredths-zoom.why: Why is {{num:1.25}} exactly halfway between {{num:1.2}} and {{num:1.3}}?
hundredths-zoom.model: {{num:1.2}} is the same as {{num:1.20}}, and {{num:1.3}} is the same as {{num:1.30}}. From 20 hundredths to 30 hundredths there are 10 parts, and 25 hundredths is 5 parts from each end.

feedback.count: Place one point on the bottom line.
feedback.too-big: Too far. Move just 5 hundredths along from {{num:1.2}}.
feedback.too-small: Go a little further. You need to move 5 small parts along from {{num:1.2}}.
